global.name: Log a line when the game starts

params.text: App Boot runs once each time the game starts, after its first page has been drawn. Log writes the line to the console, which Dev Mode shows and players never see. Anything the game should do once at start goes after this event.

params.value: Hello, World! Welcome to NarraLeaf Studio

params.text: Two sounds for the presses that sound only on a condition: an unlocked scene card, CG or recollection entry plays confirm and a locked one stays silent, and the confirm dialog plays confirm on the answer that acts and back on the others. Those blueprints call these functions with Call Fn after their check, and the Confirm page calls UI back cue when Escape backs out of a question, since a key has no element to carry a sound. A sound that always plays when an element is pressed or hovered is set in that element's Sound section instead and needs no blueprint. Both kinds play on the SFX track, so the Sound effects slider on the Config page sets their volume.

Escape and scrolling the mouse wheel down are bound to the Close the log action (Input actions panel), and this page answers it. Clear Page closes every page above the story, this one included, so the player is back in it; with no game running, Go back after it returns to the page beneath. The Back button on the left runs the same two nodes.

Runs when the page opens. Get History gives every line shown so far, Set List Content makes an Entry row for each, and Scroll To Bottom brings the newest into view. Inside a row, Speaker, Line and Avatar each show one field of that row, so this blueprint does not touch them.

log-entries-go-back.name: Go back to the pressed line

params.text: Runs when the player presses a row. Going back undoes everything after that line, so Show Confirm asks first; its question and its two answers are localization keys, looked up by the three Get Text nodes on the execution wire. On the first answer, Restore From History takes the story back to the pressed line (Get Field reads the row's id) and Go back closes this page over it. The second answer leaves the log as it was.
Ask first
Go back to that line

Runs each time the page opens. Shows Text pane, hides Sound pane and lights the Text button (Selected variant), so the page always opens on the text settings. The Text and Sound buttons switch panes the same way when pressed. To open on Sound instead, swap the two Visible values and the two variants.

Runs when the page opens. Reads the skip setting the player saved, so a returning player sees the choice they left: Read only is lit when only read text is skipped, All text otherwise. Pressing either button changes the setting and the highlight in that button's own blueprint. This is the pattern for any pair of buttons that shows a saved choice; the two layers below repeat it for full screen and for muting when unfocused.
Only read text is skipped
All text is skipped

config-show-fullscreen.name: Show whether the game is full screen

params.text: Same pattern as the skip setting, for full screen: On is lit in full screen, Off in a window. Get Fullscreen asks the game window, so it sits on the execution wire before If instead of feeding the condition by itself.
In full screen

Item Click runs when the player presses an option, with its Index (0 for the first). Select Choice takes that option of the choice the story is showing, and the story carries on down its branch. Each option draws its words from its own row: Option text shows the row's text.

Runs on the Advance action (a click, Space or Enter; Input actions panel), which this page answers while the story is on screen. With the dialogue box shown, Next moves the story on one line. With the box hidden (Hide on the quick menu, or a long press), the same press only brings the box back, so no line goes by unseen. An NVL passage reads on with the keys of the actions that move the story on here. With Next in a graph like this one, that holds from the first line; with Next in a script layer, an action counts once one of its presses has moved the dialogue box on, and an NVL passage before that reads on with a click alone.
Runs on the Backlog action (scrolling the mouse wheel up; Input actions panel) while the story is on screen. Go Page opens the Log page over the story, as the quick menu's Log button does.

Runs on the Hide action (a long press) while the story is on screen. Hide Dialog takes the dialogue box away so the whole picture can be seen; the next Advance brings it back (layer "Advance or restore the dialogue"). The quick menu's Hide button does the same with Toggle Dialog Display.

Init runs when the dialogue box appears, and On Flush each time it shows a new line. Nametag rule is shown while Get Nametag gives a name and hidden while it gives none: on a narration line, and while a choice is on screen. The plate, which is always on screen, does this for the rule inside it.

Runs each time the quick menu appears. Auto Forward is saved with the player's settings, so a player who left it on sees Auto lit (Selected variant), and otherwise dim (Default). Pressing Auto changes the setting and the highlight in that button's own blueprint.

Sets Auto Forward to the opposite of what it is, then reads it back: this button is lit (Selected variant) when Auto is now on and dim (Default) when it is off. When the menu appears, the quick menu's own blueprint shows the saved setting the same way. Skip is the same graph with the skipping nodes; a component param cannot choose which node runs, and the two buttons show different words, so they are two copies.

Skipping reads quickly through line after line; with Skip set to Read only on the Config page it stops at a line the player has not read. Auto is the same graph with the Auto Forward nodes; a component param cannot choose which node runs, and the two buttons show different words, so they are two copies.

a1a0e2ea-6c1b-4034-ac33-9ce70c9952d0.name: Continue from the latest auto save

params.text: Runs when Continue is pressed. While the game saves on its own (Automatic saving, Project panel ▸ Game), the newest auto save is where the player left off, so Load Save opens it. With no auto save, List Saves looks for the player's own saves: if there are any, Go Page opens the Load page to pick one from; with none, nothing happens.

Runs when Quit is pressed. Closing the game cannot be taken back, so Show Confirm asks first; its question and its two answers are localization keys, looked up by the three Get Text nodes on the execution wire. On the first answer, Quit Application closes the game window. The second answer leaves the title page as it was.
Ask first

The Nametag text is bound to this blueprint (Blueprint Value): what Return Value hands back is what the text shows. It runs when the dialogue box appears (Init) and each time it shows a new line (On Flush). Get Nametag gives the name of the character who is speaking, and nothing on a narration line.

86a4d04c-b01e-4b5f-95da-1f7a578e87fc.name: Show the name in the speaker's colour

params.text: Init runs when the dialogue box appears, and On Flush each time it shows a new line; each paints this text in the colour of the character who is speaking (Characters panel), or in the palette's Primary when that character has none. The name itself comes from the Nametag Blueprint Value.

Runs when the player presses one of the buttons. Close This Layer closes this page and hands the button's index, read from its row (0 for the first), back to the Show Confirm that opened it, which then runs that button's Pressed output. The first button is the answer that acts, so it plays the confirm sound; a later one backs out and plays the back sound (both are functions of the Global blueprint).

Escape is bound to the Dismiss action (Input actions panel), and this page answers it the way Cancel backs out: the back sound plays, then Close This Layer closes the page without an answer, so the Show Confirm that asked leaves through Dismissed. No question in this project does anything after Cancel or Dismissed; one that should wires both to the same nodes. While a question is up only this page hears the keys, so the page under it stays open.

Init runs when the dialogue box appears, and On Flush each time it shows a new line; each sets this image to the avatar of the character who is speaking (Characters panel). A narration line has no speaker, so the image is left empty.

Runs when the page opens. List Auto Saves reads the auto saves the game has made, and Set List Content draws one row for each, from the Auto save row inside the list. Each row's time and line are Blueprint Values on its two texts.

0792406b-10a3-438a-914d-70d316deaf0a.name: Load the auto save when pressed

params.text: Item Click runs for the row that was pressed, and Get Field reads that row's auto save. Over a running game the Confirm page asks first, because loading leaves the game the player is in, and the auto save loads only on the first answer. With no game running there is nothing to lose, so it loads at once.

init.name: Show when the auto save was made

params.text: The Blueprint Value of the row's Auto time text. It runs for each row the list draws: Get Field reads that row's auto save, and what Return Value gives back is what the text shows.

init.name: Show the line the auto save stopped on

params.text: The Blueprint Value of the row's Auto line text, run for each row the list draws. An auto save made before any line played holds an empty line, and the row shows No line instead of nothing.

Every slot on the Save and Load pages is this component, and its blueprint runs once for each slot with that slot's own Slot param: the id its save is kept under. Init draws the slot when the page opens. Saving into the slot or deleting its save calls Refresh slot again, so the slot shows the change at once. Show the save and Show an empty slot are the next two layers.

Called by Refresh slot when the slot holds a save. Each Get Save node reads one part of the save by the slot's Slot param, and the node right after it shows that part: the place, who was speaking, the line, when it was saved, how long the game had been played, and the picture taken when it was saved. Get Save Line is read twice, once for the speaker and once for the line, so that each part is read where it is shown.
Called by Refresh slot when the slot holds no save. Shows No data where the picture was and empties every text, so a slot whose save was just deleted stops showing it.
Runs when the page opens. Writes a 0 in front of the slot's Slot param, so slot 1 reads 01.

dd847eb7-8fe0-4cbf-bd83-5c02eb9fa6e5.name: Save into the slot when pressed

params.text: Runs only where the slot's Mode param is save: the slots on the Save page. An empty slot is saved into at once. A slot that already holds a save asks first, on the Confirm page, and is overwritten only on the first answer. Both ways end in Save into the slot, below: Save Game keeps a picture of the screen and writes the Location persistent variable, the place the story last set, into the save's Place field. Refresh slot then shows the new save.

Runs only where the slot's Mode param is load: the slots on the Load page. An empty slot does nothing. Over a running game the Confirm page asks first, because loading leaves the game the player is in, and the save loads only on the first answer. With no game running there is nothing to lose, so the save loads at once.

Right-clicking a slot that holds a save asks on the Confirm page, and deletes the save only on the first answer. Refresh slot then shows the slot as empty. On an empty slot nothing happens. Works the same on both pages.

Outside a game (the page was opened from the title page), Go Page set to None closes every page opened over Title and so returns there.

5107c0a1-0000-4000-8000-000000000511.name: Show the logo and the disclaimer, then open Title

params.text: Runs when the page opens. Logo fades in with the page and the first long Delay holds it; it is hidden, Disclaimer is shown and held by the second, and Title opens once Disclaimer is hidden. A long wait counts from the start of the fade in (set in each element's Animation section); the short ones let the fade out finish. Advance (a click, Space or Enter) and Dismiss (Escape) end the long wait that is running, so the element on screen fades out at once. Skip Delay reaches a Delay through its Token pin, which is why the presses are handled in this layer. Replace Page closes this page as it opens Title, so Go back and Go Page set to None return to Title, not here. Disclaimer starts hidden: show it in the UI Outline to edit it, then hide it again. For an image logo, put an Image element in Logo in place of Wordmark.

Leaves the page the way Escape does on it. Over a running game, Clear Page closes every page opened over the story, and the player is back in it. With no game running, Clear Page does nothing and Go back returns to the page this one was opened from. The Save, Load, Config, Log and Extra pages all place this one button, so what Back does is changed here, once.

Runs when this button is pressed on a row of the log. Get Field reads the row's voiceId, and Play Voice plays that line's take again in the voice language in force; a take still speaking stops first. The button is drawn only on rows whose line has a take to play: its visibility reads the row's hasVoice field.
